body: **2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff** — made the engine's changed set truthful and the tree refresh read it; the diff became one more reader of the snapshot model, no second role or name mapping. Matters: any highlight or Cells selected reading added to the tree/snapshot reaches the tree only if its move marks the changed set, and the diff reads it only through the model.

**2026-10-07-settle-detection** — a harness settle neither reads nor drains the changed set; a freshly booted document holds a non-empty set, so a check reading the set as "what one step changed" drains first (`decision/harness-settle-leaves-changed-set`). Trap for any new check that a highlight move or a Cells selection marks the set.

**2026-10-07-audit-corrections** — the stand checks' expected roles and names stated once in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs` tables, never a second mapping (`decision/role-name-tables-stated-once`). A Cells grid role or a selected cell reading extends those tables, not a local copy.

**2026-10-10-snapshot-states** (the tree states selected, toggled and invalid) — the builder writes `selected` from `aria-selected` on every element, trimmed and lower-cased, and the snapshot takes `selected` from the tree, never the element (`decision/aria-states-on-every-element`, `decision/aria-state-lower-case-closed-values`, `decision/snapshot-reads-the-tree`); ratified by the founder. The path a Cells selected cell reading would take.

**2026-10-10-snapshot-states** (the stand states a listbox, two toggle buttons and two invalid inputs) — CRUD states `role="listbox"`/`role="option"` with `aria-selected` by attribute alone, no element, key, id or Tab order moving. The precedent the scope names for Cells' selected cell (debt 5): selected stated by attribute, no focusability change.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — the snapshot text crossing to MCP ratified by the founder (2026-10-10); MCP results read the snapshot model alone. The founder's 2026-10-10 field rule the scope invokes for debt 3: a closed-value field inside a ratified carrier is no widening, a new key or open value still is.

**2026-10-12-self-description** — the node keys' help states each reading and `DiffNode::differs` names readings in node-key order, closed words only. A new highlight or selected-cell reading must be stated in the help and named by `differs`.

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** — a screenshot is one more reader of the model's bounds and changes nothing: no focus moves, `has_changes` false, next diff empty (`decision/screenshot-changes-nothing`). Today the highlighted row shows only in a shot; any fix to debt 3 must keep the shot inert.

**2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness** (`disabled` by presence, the CRUD list's keys) — the CRUD list became a Tab stop whose arrows move the selection, rows stay unfocusable options, tree focus on the list, no `aria-activedescendant`. The listbox-with-unfocusable-options pattern a select highlight reading or a Cells grid selection would mirror.

**2026-10-13-stand-contrast-harness** — built `Harness::text_contrast` (WCAG 2.x, 4.5 / 3.0 large, composited to the first opaque layer, `None` under opacity, filter, background image) and `stand_contrast`'s table (`decision/wcag-contrast-thresholds`, `decision/text-contrast-required-ratio`). The one reader a highlighted-row or chosen-row contrast fix must go through.

**2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions** (SC 1.4.3 met, three contrast tables) — stand accent darkened (`decision/stand-accent-colour`), `TEXT_ROWS` and `STATE_ROWS` read by one shared reader, SC 1.4.3 asserted on every measured non-exempt row (`decision/stand-contrast-asserted`). Any new highlighted/chosen-row contrast row joins these tables.

**2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions** (the enabled-state walks, the list named, three gaps re-homed) — the missing `aria-activedescendant` (SC 4.1.2 work outside tier 0) re-homed to a residual by the founder's F2 «Оставить записанным». Bears on debt 3: a highlight reading via active descendant is outside the tier-0 reach unless the founder widens it.

**2026-10-18-engine-debts** (§2–§4, §7: the toggle per role and the snapshot's sources) — the unread `aria-activedescendant` kept and pinned by `accessibility_active_descendant_unread` (`decision/active-descendant-unread`, `decision/active-descendant-kept-unread`), ratified 2026-10-18. A debt-3 fix reading active descendant would flip that pin.

**2026-10-18-engine-debts** (§5, §6: `inert` and `disabled`) — disabled narrowed to form controls by presence, `inert` read in focus order (`decision/disabled-by-presence`, `decision/focusable-elements`). Gates any new select/Cells key or focus path.

**2026-10-17-upstream-sync-engine-debts** — upstream's six builder reads kept, `aria-expanded` among them, with one read per ARIA attribute (`decision/one-read-per-aria-attribute`). A new select or grid reading must not add a second read of an attribute.

**2026-10-19-upstream-sync-visual-lint-and-real-app-readiness** — `:focus-within` matches, `:focus-visible` never does (`decision/focus-visible-never-matches`). Cells' focus outline is drawn with `:focus` rules; a selected-cell cue must too.

**2026-10-19-visual-lint** — the lint's `contrast` reads through `text_contrast` with the stand's exempt rule, no second formula or threshold (`decision/lint-contrast-single-formula`, `decision/lint-contrast-shares-one-reader`); stand at boot reads no contrast finding. Debt 1 must extend the lint through this one reader.

**2026-10-19-visual-lint** (the gated part) — a `contrast` finding is `id` · `defect` · `bounds` · `ratio` · `required`, ids, closed words and numbers only, ratified as the `lint` verb on every carrier (`contract/lint-contrast-finding/*`, `contract/visual-lint-finding/content`). A highlighted-row finding stays in this shape or is a widening.

Base of every select reading this chunk touches.

Debts 2 and 4.

A11y Strategy) — `~ decision/a11y-tree-refresh-on-change` and `~ decision/accessibility-tree-through-document-method`: the tree is pushed in a redraw after style resolve only when the changed set is non-empty, through the document trait's method; a poll pushes none. Five select-list and selection debts, each put to the founder as a fork first; each ruled fixed is fixed and proven headless on the stand or a fixture in both layout modes, each ruled kept is re-stated as a residual with his reason.
The debts: an open select list's highlighted row contrast (and a multiple select's chosen row) unread by the visual lint; a larger authored font clipping in the list's one-height rows; the highlighted row absent from the snapshot and the accessibility tree; a single select's size > 1 rendering as a closed dropdown instead of a list box; Cells' data cells stating no selected reading and no grid role.
Any reading added crosses the driver's carriers (snapshot, diff, MCP, kept check); a closed-value field inside a ratified carrier is no widening, a new key or open value is the founder's fork.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the select list recorded, the select model's limits retired) — recorded the open list as a ratified direct engine change for every document, remote pages included, and named its standing limits: the thumb not draggable, the highlighted row's contrast unread by the lint, a larger authored font clipping in the one row height, the highlight absent from the snapshot and the tree, a single select's `size` unread. Four of this chunk's five debts are these limits, so their fixes retire this record's limit lines. It also records the rejected designs (`:open` plus rows as boxes, a second OS window, an overlay hit in `hit_inner`, colours in `default.css`), which no fix may bring back, and the list's sixteen-file merge surface.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the list's paint and a group's header) — `paint_scene` paints the open list last through `paint_select_list`. The row text is laid out at paint through the public `select_row_layout`, only for the rows in the scrollport, which is the stated exception to paint-assumes-resolved-layout. `stroke_text_as`/`RunPaint` gives a header synthesized bold. The list colours are engine constants on `SelectListView` (`HIGHLIGHT_TEXT` #000000, `HIGHLIGHT_BACKGROUND` #c8c8c8, `DISABLED_TEXT` #6d6d6d, `BORDER` #999999), not tokens. Debt 1 (highlight contrast) reads these constants. Debt 2 (larger font) changes how rows are laid out in `packages/blitz-paint/src/render/select_list.rs`.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the list's state and placement in the engine) — `BaseDocument.select_list`, its public readers (`open_select`, `select_list_bounds`, `select_list_view`, `select_row_layout`) and crate-private machinery (`measure_select_list`, `text_row_layout`, `select_list_region`, …) in `node::select_list`. Placement is at most 20 rows (`MAX_ROWS`), opening where the rows fit, and `fresh` guards against a `:focus` restyle. This is where the one row height a larger authored font clips in is computed (debt 2). Any new reader of the highlight (debt 3) also starts here.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the list on the carriers, a boundary widening) — the list crosses the carriers only as a row's own `bounds` in the snapshot and the diff, `differs` naming `bounds`, and as pixels in a shot. The snapshot carries no `expanded` node key, `NodeState` holds no field for the list, and `NODE_FIELDS` keeps its keys (an operator's call). A highlight reading (debt 3) either stays a closed value inside this ratified crossing or is a new key/field and so a widening for the founder. The decision row select-list-crossing is the row this entry created.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (a single select's `expanded` in the tree) — a single select reads no `aria-expanded` and writes `set_expanded(open)` from its list, a closed bool of engine state read as inside the adapter's states class and outside the widening. This is the precedent for putting the highlighted row in the accessibility tree (debt 3, for example an active-descendant or selected-row state) without widening. An author's `open` on a select steers nothing.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (`size` on a `multiple` select) — F8 «Читать на multiple»: a `multiple` select's `size` hints `size` × 1.2em through `size_rows` (capped at 65534; `0` or a bad value gives no hint), with `select[multiple][size] { overflow-y: auto; }` and `line-height: 1.2` in the default sheet. A key brings the current row into view only where `size` is valid. The limit was narrowed to "a single select's `size` is unread". Debt 4 reopens this founder ruling (see also n=11).

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the list in the redraws and the changed set) — the list's open and close mark the select in the changed set, and a page scroll, a box move or a wheel elsewhere marks it on close. A highlight move or a wheel inside the list marks nothing, and a redraw is asked on open, move, scroll and close. If a highlight reading (debt 3) reaches the snapshot or the tree, it must decide whether a highlight move now marks the changed set, which today it explicitly does not.

body: The lint verb's contrast defect and its reason key: whether it reads an open select list's highlighted row and a multiple select's chosen row, today unread, and how a finding on such a row crosses on the lint answer.
The select list's colours as engine constants and the multiple select's chosen-row colours: the highlighted-row and chosen-row text and background pairs whose contrast is measured.
The open select list's row layout, row height, bounds and placement (at most 20 rows, placed where they fit), and the visible region of a list row, as a larger authored font changes them.
The lint's overlap reading of select options and list rows, and its clip and truncation defects, as they read rows sized by a larger font.

The highlighted row's reading: the snapshot node keys and state tokens (selected, expanded), the snapshot diff's differs and values, and the accessibility tree's aria-selected and single-select expanded state, for an open select list.

The select list's crossing rule: today it crosses only as bounds and pixels; any highlight reading added must ride the ratified carriers (snapshot, diff, MCP, kept check) as a closed-value field, since a new key or open value widens the boundary and is the founder's.

The select size rule: size read as a height hint on a multiple select alone; a single select with size above 1 rendered as a list box instead of a closed dropdown would change the single select's list opening, its keyboard model, row clicks and the snapshot's rows.

Cells' grid: its single Tab stop with arrow and Enter editing, its data cells keyed by author keys and the edit input's key, and whether a cell states a selected reading and a grid role in the snapshot and the accessibility tree, as the flight booker and CRUD state selected by attribute.
Every engine fix reaches every document, remote pages included: the select list and select model are direct engine changes, each flagged upstreamable, and each such change is a founder fork.
No new carrier, verb, exit code, refusal cause, session error, log field or span is planned; one only by the founder's word.
The select list's changed-set marks and resolve's reconciling of the list, which a new reading of the highlighted row must keep in step so the diff and the accessibility refresh see it.
The select list painted inside the scene and its painting order over the page, which the highlighted-row and chosen-row painting under a larger font must keep.
The test harness's contrast ratio and text contrast readers, and its screenshot, as the measurement of the highlight's and chosen row's contrast.
The stand's typography and pinned environment (DejaVu Sans, readings identical on every CI OS), under which a larger-font row height is measured.

The founder forks are written into one file in the run dir, each with its measurement, every option with its cost, the recommended option first and the forks' dependencies; technical forks that turn nothing of the product are the operator's.
Each fix proven headless on the stand or a fixture in both layout modes; each kept debt stands as a residual with the founder's reason.
